findings.title: Unresolved findings escape the gate: stage_id relabelling and dropped findings are not detected
findings.reproduction: tools/gates/lib/rules.mjs:278 evaluates the terminal-state rule only for findings whose stage_id === the gate's stage; rules.mjs:275-277 only cross-checks finding IDs listed by the gate's final PASS records; stages.json review_rounds[].records and the <role>.findings.json sidecars of earlier (FAIL) rounds are never consulted; tools/gates/import-findings.mjs:42-51 imports sidecar findings without checking f.stage_id against --stage. Scenario A: round-1 code-security FAIL raises F-DG0-1xx (High, mandatory, OPEN); its stage_id is set (or imported) as 'DG1' -> validate.mjs --stage DG0 PASSes with the finding still OPEN. Scenario B: the OPEN finding is simply never imported / removed from findings.json; the round-2 PASS records do not list it -> the gate PASSes. Reproduction script (static, not executed - Bash unavailable in this run): docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG0/code-security/repro.test.mjs tests R1a and R1b.
findings.expected: Every finding raised in any review round of the stage (all review_rounds records and their findings sidecars) must exist in findings.json with stage_id equal to the stage and be in a terminal state with independent verification; a finding cannot be deferred to another stage by relabelling without an explicit, audited transfer.
findings.actual: A High mandatory-violation finding raised at DG0 can remain OPEN (relabelled stage_id) or be absent from findings.json and validate.mjs --stage DG0 still exits 0, bypassing the 'zero unresolved Critical/High and mandatory findings' gate condition.

findings.title: Invocation provenance is satisfied by a fabricated 4-field meta.json; transcript and result are never checked
findings.reproduction: tools/gates/lib/rules.mjs:225-235 (checkInvocation) reads only runs/<stage>/<run_id>/meta.json and checks role, invocation_reference.session_id, exit_code and is_error. It does not require transcript.jsonl.gz or result.json to exist, does not compare meta.result_session_id (written by run-agent.sh:77) to the requested session, does not bind the record's 'assignment' to meta.assignment/assignment_sha256, does not check meta.task/stage or that the run started after candidate.frozen_at, and run-agent.sh:66-89 records no hash of the transcript. The validator's own fixture (tools/gates/tests/validator.test.mjs:60-67) proves a hand-written {run_id, role, invocation_reference:{session_id}, exit_code:0, is_error:false} passes. Scenario: anyone with repo write access (Bash is unguarded for every role) writes docs/delivery/runs/DG0/DG0-x/meta.json for each role plus four PASS review records and a gate record -> validate.mjs --stage DG0 and --pipeline (historical) exit 0 with no agent ever invoked. Historical mode (rules.mjs:341-395) re-reads these mutable, candidate-excluded files from the working tree, so approvals can also be rewritten after the fact. Repro: docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG0/code-security/repro.test.mjs R0 (not executed in this run).
findings.expected: The validator refuses a review/audit/verification unless the referenced run has transcript.jsonl.gz and result.json present, meta records a SHA-256 of the transcript that matches, the transcript's init/result lines carry the same session_id, result_session_id equals the requested session_id, the run's assignment path/SHA matches the record's assignment file, meta.stage equals the gate stage, and the run started after the candidate froze.
findings.actual: Provenance (DG0 approval condition 'required stage agents actually invoked', A23/A24) can be satisfied entirely with fabricated metadata; the check does not raise the cost of forgery beyond writing one small JSON file.

findings.title: Symlinks and submodule gitlinks are silently excluded from the candidate identity, contrary to D-005
findings.reproduction: tools/gates/lib/candidate.mjs:70 skips any working-tree path that is not a regular file (lstat, so symlinks are dropped) and candidate.mjs:83 skips tree entries with mode 120000 (symlink) and all non-blob entries (gitlinks/submodules). D-005 defines the candidate as 'every tracked and untracked-not-ignored file'. Scenario: a committed symlink src/entry.txt -> app.txt is part of the approved deliverable; after approval it is repointed to ../docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG0/payload.txt (excluded metadata, writable by reviewers) or to any other target -> manifestFromWorkingTree hashes identically and validate.mjs --stage DG0 still PASSes although the effective deliverable changed; the frozen manifest never lists the symlink so reviewers cannot see it. Repro: repro.test.mjs R2 (not executed in this run).
findings.expected: Symlinks are hashed by their link target string (e.g. entry 'symlink:<target>') and gitlinks by their commit OID, or their presence fails candidate computation; the manifest lists them.
findings.actual: Any symlink or submodule in the tree is invisible to candidate identity and to the change detection that A25 relies on.

findings.title: The frozen manifest's spec is not bound to stages.json candidate_spec or to the D-005 exclusion policy
findings.reproduction: rules.mjs:315-331 recomputes the candidate using manifest.spec, read from docs/delivery/candidates/<DGx>.manifest.json (itself candidate-excluded metadata). Nothing checks manifest.spec against stages.json candidate_spec, and nothing restricts exclude globs to the D-005 set (trading_agent/** + META_EXCLUDES). stages.json candidate_spec is also excluded metadata, so changing it never changes any candidate. Scenario: a manifest frozen with spec.exclude ['src/**'] (or 'apps/**') -> later edits and new files under src/ never change the recomputed ID and validate.mjs --stage keeps PASSing. Repro: repro.test.mjs R3 (not executed in this run).
findings.expected: The validator requires manifest.spec to equal the stage's candidate_spec and rejects exclude patterns beyond the approved policy (or requires a decision record for each), so exclusions cannot silently hide deliverables.
findings.actual: Arbitrary exclusions in the manifest are accepted; the only safeguard is a human reviewer noticing the spec.

findings.title: Write guard: protected list omits Claude configuration surfaces and trading_agent/, and paths are checked lexically (symlinks followed)
findings.reproduction: (1) tools/agents/write-scopes.json:3-17 protects .claude/settings.json but not .claude/settings.local.json, .mcp.json, .claude/hooks/** or .claude/commands/**, and does not protect trading_agent/** (CLAUDE.md: 'Do not modify it'; also excluded from every candidate, so edits there are invisible to gates). An implementer (allow '**') may Write .claude/settings.local.json, which Claude Code loads into every later project session, including guarded agent runs; per Claude Code settings documentation a 'disableAllHooks': true there would disable the PreToolUse guard for all later runs (not reproduced end-to-end: running claude is out of scope for this review). (2) guard-write.mjs:52-54 resolves the target lexically with path.resolve and never calls realpath, so a Write to docs/analysis/lnk/lib/rules.mjs, where docs/analysis/lnk -> ../../tools/gates, is ALLOWED for transformation-analyst while it lands in tools/gates. (3) Matching is case-sensitive: on case-insensitive filesystems (macOS/Windows) 'Tools/Gates/x' bypasses the deny list. Policy context: Bash is not path-guarded for any role (all ten definitions include Bash); this is disclosed in agent-protocol.md:75, agents.md:69 and D-009, and the compensating control is the orchestrator's git status check. Repro: repro.test.mjs R6 (not executed in this run).
findings.expected: Deny list includes .claude/** (except none), .mcp.json and trading_agent/** for implementers; the guard canonicalises the target with fs.realpathSync on the deepest existing ancestor and denies if either the lexical or the real path is protected; comparisons are case-folded on case-insensitive platforms.
findings.actual: Implementers can write Claude configuration that governs later guarded sessions and the unrelated user project; symlinked paths bypass deny rules.

findings.title: Evidence-existence checks accept directories, '#fragment' and non-path strings; gate tests[] may be empty
findings.reproduction: rules.mjs:255-258 and :391 use existsSync(join(repo, ev.split('#')[0])): '#x' and '.' resolve to the repo root and pass; a directory passes as evidence. rules.mjs:190-191 only checks register evidence entries that contain '/', so evidence 'done' passes for an IMPLEMENTED DG0 row. rules.mjs:258 accepts assignment '.'. gate.schema.json:97 has no minItems on tests, so a gate with zero recorded tests passes. Repro: repro.test.mjs R0/R4 (not executed in this run).
findings.expected: Evidence and assignment must resolve to an existing regular file inside the repo (not the root, not outside it); register evidence tokens must be paths or explicitly typed references; a gate records at least the stage's required checks.
findings.actual: Placeholder evidence satisfies the 'linked evidence' condition.

findings.title: CSV handling silently accepts malformed input (text after closing quote; extra cells dropped by merge)
findings.reproduction: tools/gates/lib/csv.mjs:13-22: after a closing quote, following characters are appended to the field, so '"x"y,z' parses as 'xy' instead of being rejected as non-RFC-4180. tools/source/merge_register.py:27/43: csv.DictReader stores surplus cells under key None and DictWriter writes only header keys, so a part-file row with an unquoted comma loses its trailing cells silently (short rows become empty strings). The validator's empty-column rule catches only non-optional columns. Repro: repro.test.mjs R5 (not executed in this run).
findings.expected: Parser throws on characters between a closing quote and the next delimiter; merge fails on rows whose cell count differs from the header.
findings.actual: Malformed rows are accepted with altered content.

findings.title: Runner hygiene: unvalidated --stage/--task/--role, second-resolution run IDs can overwrite evidence
findings.reproduction: tools/agents/run-agent.sh:17-39: STAGE, TASK and ROLE are used unvalidated in filesystem paths (OUT=runs/$STAGE/$RUN_ID; a --stage containing '../' writes evidence outside runs/) and in RUN_ID, which may then not match the schema pattern ^DG[0-7]-[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$. RUN_ID has one-second resolution and 'mkdir -p' reuses an existing directory, so two runs of the same role/task started in the same second overwrite each other's transcript/meta. No shell injection found: all values are quoted and passed to python via argv with a quoted heredoc; the prompt is a single argument.
findings.expected: Validate --stage against ^DG[0-7]$ and --task/--role against a safe charset; include the session UUID (or a mkdir without -p that fails on existence) in the run directory.
findings.actual: Evidence directories can collide or be misplaced by argument mistakes.

findings.title: CI actions pinned to mutable major tags rather than commit SHAs
findings.reproduction: .github/workflows/delivery-gates.yml:18 'actions/checkout@v4' and :21 'actions/setup-node@v4' resolve to whatever the tag points to at run time; a moved tag changes the code that runs the gate job. Otherwise the workflow is sound: permissions contents: read, fetch-depth: 0 for historical checks, no secrets referenced, and every step's non-zero exit fails the job.
findings.expected: Third-party actions pinned by full commit SHA (with the tag in a comment).
